symptom: PC in Sales department cannot reach any other PC in Sales, but can ping its own gateway.
cli_snippet:
show vlan brief
VLAN Name        Status  Ports
10  Sales        active  Fa0/1,Fa0/2,Fa0/3,Fa0/4
20  HR           active  Fa0/6,Fa0/7
(Fa0/5 not listed under VLAN 10)

show interfaces fa0/5 switchport
Administrative Mode: static access
Operational Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 20 (HR)
root_cause: Port Fa0/5 is assigned to VLAN 20 (HR) instead of VLAN 10 (Sales), isolating the PC from its intended broadcast domain.
outcome: Access port reassigned to VLAN 10. Sales PC regained connectivity, verified with ping to a peer.

symptom: Devices on SW2 in VLAN 30 cannot communicate with devices on VLAN 30 connected to SW1, even though both switches show VLAN 30 active.
cli_snippet:
show interfaces trunk (SW1)
Port  Native vlan
Gi0/1  1

show interfaces trunk (SW2)
Port  Native vlan
Gi0/1  99

%CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH: Native VLAN mismatch discovered on Gi0/1
root_cause: Native VLAN mismatch on the trunk link (VLAN 1 on SW1 vs VLAN 99 on SW2) is causing untagged traffic to leak between VLANs and breaking inter-switch communication.
fix_step_2: switchport trunk native vlan 99  ! apply consistently on SW1 to match SW2
outcome: Native VLAN aligned to 99 on both switches. CDP warning cleared and cross-switch VLAN 30 traffic resumed.

symptom: New laptops joining the network cannot obtain an IP address; ipconfig shows a 169.254.x.x address.
cli_snippet:
show ip dhcp pool SALES
Pool SALES :
 Utilization mark (high/low)    : 100 / 0
 Total addresses                : 50
 Leased addresses               : 50
root_cause: The DHCP pool for VLAN 10 is fully exhausted (50/50 leases used), so new clients fail to lease an address and self-assign an APIPA address.
fix_step_2: network 192.168.10.0 255.255.254.0  ! expand pool or shorten lease time
outcome: DHCP pool expanded. New laptops received valid leases within seconds.

symptom: Hosts on VLAN 40 (a subnet with no local DHCP server) never receive an IP address from the central DHCP server on VLAN 1.
cli_snippet:
show run interface vlan 40
interface Vlan40
 ip address 192.168.40.1 255.255.255.0
(no ip helper-address configured)
root_cause: Vlan40 interface is missing the 'ip helper-address' command, so DHCP broadcasts from VLAN 40 clients are never relayed to the DHCP server on VLAN 1.
outcome: ip helper-address added to Vlan40. DHCP requests now relayed and VLAN 40 hosts obtained addresses.

symptom: All hosts on the Finance subnet can ping internal servers but cannot reach any website by name, though pinging the website's IP works fine.
cli_snippet:
ipconfig /all (Finance-PC1)
DNS Servers . . . . . . . . . . : 10.10.10.50

ping 10.10.10.50
Request timed out.
root_cause: The configured DNS server (10.10.10.50) is unreachable, so name resolution fails while direct IP connectivity still works.
fix_step_2: dns-server 10.10.10.51  ! point to a reachable DNS server
outcome: DNS server address corrected. Name resolution verified with nslookup and a browser test.

symptom: A single PC in the Marketing VLAN cannot reach any device outside its own subnet, but can ping other PCs in the same VLAN.
cli_snippet:
ipconfig (Marketing-PC5)
IPv4 Address. . . . . . . . . . . : 192.168.20.15
Default Gateway . . . . . . . . . : 192.168.20.254
root_cause: The PC's default gateway is manually set to 192.168.20.254, which does not exist on this subnet; the real gateway is 192.168.20.1, so all off-subnet traffic is dropped.
fix_step_1: On host: set default gateway to 192.168.20.1
outcome: Gateway corrected to 192.168.20.1 on the host. Off-subnet connectivity restored, verified with ping.

symptom: Two PCs on the same VLAN intermittently lose connectivity and Windows shows an 'IP address conflict' warning.
cli_snippet:
show ip arp | include 192.168.10.20
Internet  192.168.10.20   -   0018.d3aa.1122  ARPA  Vlan10
Internet  192.168.10.20   -   0022.55bb.9f10  ARPA  Vlan10
root_cause: Two devices are statically configured with the same IP address (192.168.10.20), causing an IP conflict and intermittent connectivity for both.
fix_step_1: Reassign one printer to 192.168.10.21 and update static config
outcome: Duplicate IP resolved by reassigning one printer. ARP conflict warning cleared.

symptom: Branch office PCs cannot reach the HQ server subnet (10.0.99.0/24); everything else works.
cli_snippet:
show ip route
S    192.168.1.0/24 [1/0] via 10.0.0.2
C    10.0.0.0/30 is directly connected, Serial0/0/0
(no route to 10.0.99.0/24)
root_cause: R1's routing table has no static route to the HQ server subnet 10.0.99.0/24, so traffic to that destination is dropped at the branch router.
outcome: Static route to 10.0.99.0/24 added on R1. HQ server subnet reachable, verified with traceroute.

symptom: R1 and R2 are directly connected but their OSPF neighbor relationship never gets past the INIT state.
cli_snippet:
show ip ospf neighbor (R1)
Neighbor ID  State     Address
2.2.2.2      INIT/DR   10.0.0.2

R2: network 10.0.0.0 0.0.0.3 area 1
root_cause: R2's OSPF network statement places its interface in area 1 while R1's interface is in area 0, an area mismatch that prevents the neighbor adjacency from progressing past INIT.
fix_step_2: network 10.0.0.0 0.0.0.3 area 0  ! on R2, correct the area ID
outcome: Area corrected to 0 on R2's interface. Neighbor adjacency advanced to FULL.

symptom: OSPF neighbor between R2 and R3 keeps flapping between FULL and DOWN every 40-60 seconds.
cli_snippet:
R2: Hello 10, Dead 40
R3: Hello 5, Dead 20
root_cause: Mismatched OSPF hello and dead timers between R2 and R3 (10/40 vs 5/20) are causing the neighbor's dead timer to expire repeatedly, flapping the adjacency.
fix_step_3: ip ospf dead-interval 40  ! apply on R3 to match R2
outcome: Hello/dead timers matched on R3. Neighbor relationship stabilized, no more flapping.

symptom: R1 and R2 are both configured for EIGRP but never form a neighbor relationship.
cli_snippet:
R1: router eigrp 100
R2: router eigrp 200
root_cause: R1 and R2 are configured with different EIGRP autonomous system numbers (100 vs 200); EIGRP requires matching AS numbers to form a neighbor adjacency.
fix_step_2: router eigrp 100  ! on R2, match R1's AS number
outcome: EIGRP AS corrected to 100 on R2. Neighbors established, routes appeared in the table within 30 seconds.

symptom: Employees in the Guest VLAN can browse the internet but the IT monitoring server cannot ping or poll any guest device.
cli_snippet:
show access-lists 101
Extended IP access list 101
 10 deny ip any any
root_cause: Access-list 101 consists of a single 'deny ip any any' with no permit entries above it, blocking all traffic including legitimate monitoring from the IT server.
outcome: Permit entry added for the IT monitoring server. SNMP polling and ping restored.

symptom: Internal hosts on 192.168.1.0/24 cannot reach the internet even though the router has a valid default route to the ISP.
cli_snippet:
ip nat inside source list 1 interface GigabitEthernet0/1 overload
access-list 1 permit 192.168.2.0 0.0.0.255
root_cause: The NAT access-list (ACL 1) permits the wrong subnet (192.168.2.0/24) instead of the actual internal LAN 192.168.1.0/24, so LAN traffic never matches the NAT rule and isn't translated.
outcome: NAT ACL corrected to match the LAN subnet. Internet access restored for all internal hosts.

symptom: An externally-hosted internal web server (192.168.1.100) is unreachable from the internet, though it works fine internally.
cli_snippet:
ip nat inside source static 192.168.1.101 203.0.113.10
(web server's actual IP is 192.168.1.100)
root_cause: The static NAT entry maps the public IP to 192.168.1.101 instead of the web server's real address 192.168.1.100 — a typo in the inside local address.
fix_step_1: no ip nat inside source static 192.168.1.101 203.0.113.10
outcome: Static NAT entry corrected to the actual server IP. Web server now reachable from the internet.

symptom: A user's PC loses network connectivity the moment they plug in a personal wireless router to their switch port.
cli_snippet:
show interfaces fa0/12 status
Fa0/12 err-disabled

SecurityViolation Count : 1, Violation Mode: Shutdown
root_cause: Port security detected a second MAC address on Fa0/12 (from the personal router) and, with violation mode set to shutdown, placed the port into err-disabled state.
fix_step_3: no shutdown  ! after removing the unauthorized device
outcome: Unauthorized device removed and the port re-enabled. Port security violation cleared.

symptom: Users on the Engineering floor experience random, brief network outages every few minutes even though no cables were unplugged.
cli_snippet:
%SPANTREE-2-LOOPGUARD_BLOCK: Loop guard blocking port Gi0/2 on VLAN10
%SPANTREE-2-ROOTGUARD_BLOCK: Port Gi0/1 tried to become root
root_cause: A spanning-tree topology change is being triggered repeatedly, likely from an unstable redundant link causing recurring TCN events and temporary MAC table flushes across the switches.
fix_step_1: Check physical cabling on the flapping link; consider spanning-tree portfast on edge ports only
outcome: Unstable redundant link stabilized. STP topology changes stopped, no more brief outages.

symptom: File transfers between two servers on the same switch are extremely slow and show high error counts, though the link light is up.
cli_snippet:
Gi0/3: Half-duplex, 100Mb/s
5000 input errors, 4800 CRC, 200 collisions
root_cause: A duplex mismatch exists between the server NIC (forced full-duplex) and the switch port (auto-negotiated to half-duplex), producing excessive collisions and CRC errors that slow throughput.
fix_step_3: speed 100  ! match server NIC settings on both ends
outcome: Duplex and speed matched on both ends. CRC errors and collisions dropped to zero.

symptom: A specific large file transfer over a site-to-site VPN tunnel always stalls partway through, while small transfers work fine.
cli_snippet:
Tunnel0 MTU 1476 bytes
ping size 1500 df-bit
%Error: fragmentation needed but DF bit set
root_cause: The GRE tunnel's effective MTU (1476) is smaller than the packets being sent with the Don't Fragment bit set, silently black-holing larger packets instead of fragmenting them.
outcome: TCP MSS adjusted on the tunnel. Large file transfers now complete without stalling.

symptom: A newly cabled PC shows no link light at all and gets no network access whatsoever.
cli_snippet:
show interfaces fa0/8
FastEthernet0/8 is administratively down, line protocol is down
root_cause: Interface Fa0/8 has been administratively shut down (likely left disabled from a previous configuration), preventing any link from coming up.
outcome: Interface re-enabled with no shutdown. Link came up immediately.

symptom: A newly added PC in the 192.168.5.0/26 subnet cannot reach any other device, including its own gateway, despite correct cabling and VLAN.
cli_snippet:
ipconfig
IPv4 Address: 192.168.5.70
Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0
Default Gateway: 192.168.5.65
root_cause: The PC is still configured with the old /24 subnet mask instead of the new /26 mask, so it calculates the wrong network range and cannot reach the gateway or any other host on the /26 subnet.
fix_step_1: On host: set subnet mask to 255.255.255.192
outcome: Subnet mask corrected to /26 on the host. Gateway and peer connectivity restored.

symptom: A PC connected to a port that should be a normal access port is receiving tagged VLAN frames and its NIC shows connectivity issues.
cli_snippet:
show interfaces fa0/15 switchport
Administrative Mode: trunk
Operational Mode: trunk
root_cause: Fa0/15 was never reconfigured back to access mode after being repurposed, so it is still operating as a trunk port and sending tagged frames to an end-user device.
outcome: Port reconfigured to access mode. End-user device regained normal connectivity.

symptom: Hosts in the OSPF domain (Building A) can reach hosts in the EIGRP domain (Building B) but not the reverse.
cli_snippet:
router eigrp 100
 redistribute ospf 1 metric 10000 100 255 1 1500

router ospf 1
(no redistribute eigrp statement present)
root_cause: Redistribution is configured one-way only (OSPF routes into EIGRP), so EIGRP routes are never advertised into OSPF, making Building B unreachable from Building A.
outcome: Two-way redistribution configured. Building B now reachable from Building A.

symptom: Employee laptops cannot see the corporate Wi-Fi network 'Corp-Secure' in their list of available networks at all.
cli_snippet:
show wlan 1
Status: Disabled
Broadcast SSID: Disabled
root_cause: The Corp-Secure WLAN is administratively disabled on the controller, so it is not being broadcast and cannot appear in any client's available network list.
outcome: WLAN re-enabled and SSID broadcast turned on. Corp-Secure now visible to clients.

symptom: Wireless users near the break room report frequent disconnections and very slow speeds, while users elsewhere in the building are fine.
cli_snippet:
AP3 802.11b/g/n Channel: 6
AP4 802.11b/g/n Channel: 6
root_cause: AP3 and AP4 have overlapping coverage and are both set to the same channel (6), causing co-channel interference that degrades performance for nearby clients.
fix_step_2: channel 11  ! stagger channels between overlapping APs
outcome: AP4 moved to channel 11. Interference cleared, wireless performance restored.

symptom: A VLAN created on SW1 does not appear in the VLAN database on SW2 or SW3, even though all three switches are trunked together.
cli_snippet:
SW1 VTP Domain Name: CorpNet
SW2 VTP Domain Name: corpnet
root_cause: VTP domain names are case-sensitive and do not match between SW1 ('CorpNet') and SW2 ('corpnet'), so VTP updates are rejected and the new VLAN never propagates.
fix_step_1: vtp domain CorpNet  ! run on SW2 to match SW1 exactly, including case
outcome: VTP domain name corrected to match exactly. Switch-2 now shows all VLANs from Switch-1.

symptom: After R1 (the primary gateway router) is powered off for maintenance, hosts lose their default gateway entirely instead of failing over.
cli_snippet:
R2: show standby brief
Interface  Grp  State    Virtual IP
Gi0/0      2    Standby  192.168.1.1
root_cause: R2 is configured in HSRP group 2 while R1 (now offline) was in group 1, a group number mismatch that prevents R2 from taking over the shared virtual IP when R1 fails.
fix_step_2: standby 1 ip 192.168.1.1  ! on R2, correct the group number to 1
outcome: Standby group corrected to 1 on R2. Gateway failover verified after R1 was taken offline.

symptom: An EtherChannel bundle between SW1 and SW2 fails to form; both physical links stay up individually but no Port-channel interface comes up.
cli_snippet:
SW1: channel-group 1 mode active
SW2: channel-group 1 mode on
root_cause: SW1's ports are set to LACP 'active' mode while SW2's ports are set to static 'on' mode; these modes are incompatible, so the channel never negotiates and both ports remain independent.
fix_step_2: channel-group 1 mode active  ! on SW2, match SW1's LACP mode
outcome: LACP mode matched on both switches. Port-channel formed and traffic load-balanced across both links.

symptom: R1's eBGP session to the ISP router never reaches the Established state.
cli_snippet:
show ip bgp summary
Neighbor 203.0.113.1  AS 65003  State: Idle
root_cause: R1 is configured to peer with the ISP using the wrong remote AS number (65003 instead of the correct 65002), so the BGP session cannot establish.
outcome: Remote AS corrected to 65002. BGP session reached Established state.

symptom: Hosts with valid IPv6 addresses cannot ping each other across R1, even though IPv6 addresses are configured on all interfaces.
cli_snippet:
show run | include ipv6 unicast-routing
(no output - command not present)
root_cause: IPv6 unicast routing has not been enabled globally on R1 ('ipv6 unicast-routing' is missing), so the router will not forward IPv6 packets between VLANs despite interfaces having addresses.
outcome: IPv6 unicast routing enabled on R1. Hosts across VLANs now ping successfully over IPv6.

symptom: The central log server stops receiving any messages from R1, though R1 is configured to send logs there.
cli_snippet:
logging host 10.10.5.20
access-list 110
 10 permit tcp any any eq 22
 20 deny ip any any
root_cause: ACL 110 on the outbound interface has no permit entry for UDP 514, so the 'deny ip any any' at the end silently blocks all syslog traffic to the log server.
outcome: Permit rule added for UDP 514. Syslog server began receiving messages from R1 again.
